- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast shows strong upward bias, apply downward correction of 3–5% to prevent false optimism.  
- Model tends to overestimate mid-term (10–20 day) price increases after recent spikes; cap forecast growth at 2–3% above prior 5-day average.  
- In periods of high sentiment, true outcomes often lag forecast by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to reflect 1-day lagged true value for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is rising sharply (e.g., 0.8–0.9), forecast should be slightly conservative; reduce 3–5% from peak to avoid “sentiment-driven overshoot.”  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast exceeds 20% above recent 10-day average, apply downward pressure to align with historical mean reversion pattern.
